Extended-Hours US Equity Data Moves to Pyth Pro
Extended-hours US equity feeds (.PRE, .POST, .ON) move from Pyth Core to Pyth Pro on June 15th.
Here's what changes and how to migrate.
On June 15th 2026, Pyth Core will deprecate all extended-hours and session-based US equity feeds — pre-market (.PRE), post-market (.POST), and overnight (.ON).
The full list of affected tickers is in the developer forum post.
Applications relying on these feeds should transition to Pyth Pro before June 15th to maintain access.
This change applies to roughly 50 US equity tickers across all three session categories, including AAPL, TSLA, NVDA, COIN, MSTR, META, SPY, QQQ, and others.
Regular-session feeds for these tickers remain on Pyth Core through the broader Core upgrade on July 31st.
What to do
Applications using any of the affected .PRE, .POST, or .ON feeds need to:
- Sign up for Pyth Terminal at app.pyth.com
- Subscribe to a Pyth Pro plan that includes US equities — either the U.S.
Equities plan ($5,000 / month) or All Asset Classes ($10,000 / month)
- Generate an API key and update integrations to point to the new endpoint
The full session-feed catalog and updated symbol mappings are available on Pyth Terminal.
For chain or feed support questions, email data@dourolabs.xyz.
Why this is moving
Extended-hours and overnight equity data is some of the most premium data in the legacy market data economy.
Pre-market, post-market, and overnight pricing for US equities is tightly licensed, expensive to source, and historically reserved for institutional desks paying through dedicated vendor contracts.
Pyth is one of the only providers offering true 24/5 US equity pricing onchain at all.
That coverage exists because of the network's institutional publisher base — firms with direct access to extended-hours liquidity in venues like Blue Ocean ATS, where overnight US equity trading happens.
Aggregating that data and pricing it as a paid product brings Pyth in line with how the rest of the market data world treats this category.
This is consistent with the broader Pyth Core upgrade launching on July 31st: the most valuable feeds and the highest-quality data flow through Pyth Pro, with revenue accruing to the Pyth DAO.
What stays on Pyth Core
Regular trading session equity feeds remain available on Pyth Core through July 31st, when the broader Core upgrade takes effect.
After July 31st, all Pyth Core data access requires an active Starter or Pro plan through Pyth Terminal.
The publishers are the same.
The data quality is the same.
What changes is the commercial relationship — and which Pyth product carries which category of data.
Getting started
Sign up for a Pyth Pro plan at app.pyth.com.
Read the migration documentation.

The NVIDIA CORP / US DOLLAR (Equity.US.NVDA/USD) price feed delivers a live NVDA price, updated in real time on Pyth Network.
Prices are aggregated from first-party publishers - exchanges, market makers and trading firms pricing from their own order flow - with a confidence interval on every update.
Available on 100+ blockchains.
US equities do not trade continuously.
Each weekday cycle is split into four sessions with different venues, participants and liquidity: overnight (8:00 PM-4:00 AM ET, Sunday-Thursday, on alternative trading systems such as Blue Ocean ATS), pre-market (4:00-9:30 AM ET), regular hours (9:30 AM-4:00 PM ET, with opening and closing auctions on the primary listing exchange and LULD circuit breakers active) and post-market (4:00-8:00 PM ET, typically with wider spreads, and the window in which many companies release earnings).
From Friday 8:00 PM to Sunday 8:00 PM ET no session runs, a 48-hour gap.
Within the regular session, trading is fragmented across many registered exchanges, dark pools and alternative trading systems, with the SIP consolidating exchange quotes into the NBBO.
Each stock has a primary listing venue, usually NYSE or NASDAQ, which runs its opening and closing auctions.
Pyth US equity prices are contributed directly by first-party institutions that make markets, run venues or route order flow in the stock.
Every update carries a price and a confidence interval, and consumers pull the latest price on demand instead of waiting for a scheduled push.
Publisher prices are benchmarked against the mid-point at the stock's primary listing venue.
On Pyth Pro, supported tickers are priced across all four sessions, and every update carries a marketSession field so risk logic can be session-aware.
Unlike crypto, which trades 24/7, US equity trading activity is fragmented across multiple venues and four distinct trading sessions within each 24-hour cycle.
Each session may have different participants, liquidity profiles and venues, which directly impacts how prices are formed and how much they can move.
| Tier | Participants | Role in price formation |
|---|---|---|
| Primary listing exchanges (NYSE, NASDAQ) | Designated or registered market makers, institutional and retail flow during regular hours | Run each stock's opening and closing auctions; the reference venue for Pyth's publisher benchmark |
| Other registered exchanges (including Cboe, IEX and MEMX) | Broker-dealers, market makers | Contribute quotes to the NBBO; share of volume varies by venue and by stock |
| Dark pools and alternative trading systems (ATS) | Institutional block flow; overnight venues | Off-exchange matching; the overnight session (8:00 PM-4:00 AM ET, Sunday-Thursday) trades on alternative trading systems |
| SIP (Securities Information Processor) | Quotes from all registered exchanges | Consolidates exchange quotes into the NBBO, the best bid and offer across registered exchanges |
Venues do not contribute equally to price discovery.
A price taken from one venue reflects that venue's quotes and liquidity, not the market as a whole.
| Session/Window | Time (ET) | Character |
|---|---|---|
A price gap occurs when a stock opens at a significantly different price from its previous session's close.
Because each of the four sessions has a different liquidity profile and participant base, price information does not flow smoothly across boundaries.
The resulting gaps are a structural feature of equity markets, not anomalies.
| Factor | Impact |
|---|---|
| Earnings | Often released after the 4:00 PM ET close, so the initial move forms in the post-market session on thinner liquidity |
| Company, sector and macro news | Contract awards, guidance changes, regulatory decisions and macro data can move a stock sharply in the overnight or pre-market sessions |
| Analyst upgrades/downgrades | Rating changes and large disclosed positions can trigger multi-day volatility.
Pre-market reactions can set the tone before RTH |
| Weekend / holiday gaps | The 48-hour weekend void (Friday 8:00 PM-Sunday 8:00 PM ET) is the longest scheduled closure of a normal week.
The overnight session from the Sunday open provides the first price signal |
| LULD halts | Limit Up-Limit Down circuit breakers pause trading during RTH when price moves too fast.
On resumption, price can gap up or down |
| Corporate actions | Stock splits, reverse splits and delistings create planned price discontinuities.
A 4:1 split drops the price 75% overnight: not a market move, but a structural repricing that must be handled explicitly |
Worked example.
A company reports quarterly results after the 4:00 PM ET close.
The first prices reacting to the print form in the post-market session, on thinner liquidity and wider spreads, and the next regular-session open is a gap against the prior 4:00 PM close rather than a continuation of it.
If the move is large enough to trip an LULD band after the open, trading pauses: no trades, no feed updates, and a discontinuous price on resumption.
Neither event is an anomaly; both are the normal mechanics of a four-session market.
Liquidity in US equities is not a single number.
It is typically deepest in the regular session, when market makers quote across every exchange and the SIP consolidates exchange quotes, and it thins outside it.
The windows where liquidity disappears or degrades are:
| Event | What happens |
|---|---|
| LULD halt | Trading pauses during regular hours when price breaches its band.
No trades and no feed updates while halted; price free to gap on resumption |
| After-hours earnings | The initial move forms in the post-market session, on thinner liquidity and wider spreads, before the next regular open |
| Stock split | A planned discontinuity.
Publishers apply the split ratio before the ex-date session opens, under the workflow in the Asset-Specific Handling section |
| Weekend void, every week | 48 hours (Friday 8:00 PM-Sunday 8:00 PM ET) with no session.
Positions held through the weekend carry gap risk across the longest closure of the week |

About Solana (SOL)
Solana is a high-performance Layer 1 blockchain built for mass adoption, offering a fast and low-cost environment for decentralized applications.
-
It utilizes a unique timestamping mechanism to process thousands of transactions per second with sub-second finality — the time it takes for a transaction to be fully confirmed and irreversible.
-
Users pay minimal fees, often costing a fraction of a penny, making the network accessible for frequent use and micro-transactions.
-
The platform supports a vast ecosystem of tools ranging from decentralized finance to digital collectibles and real-world assets.
What Is Solana
Solana is a decentralized computing platform designed to scale globally without the need for complex layers or sharding — a method that splits the network into pieces to process more data.
Value moves through the system via its native token, SOL, which acts as the "gas" or compute power required to execute transactions.
The token is put to work through staking, where users lock up their assets to help validators secure the network in exchange for rewards.
As the ecosystem grows, demand for SOL increases to cover transaction fees and governance — the process where token holders vote on changes to the system.
What Makes Solana Unique
-
Proof of History: This is a decentralized clock that creates a verifiable record of when events happen, allowing the network to process data much faster without constant node communication.
-
Single-Layer Scaling: Solana maintains a single, unified ledger to avoid the liquidity fragmentation often found in multi-layer or modular systems.
-
Parallel Execution: The network uses the Sealevel engine, which allows many smart contracts — automated digital agreements — to run at the exact same time.
-
Gulf Stream: A protocol that forwards transactions to validators before the previous block is finished, reducing confirmation times and memory pressure.
What Can You Use Solana for?
-
Launchpads: Solana's high speed, scalability, and low transaction costs make it one of the most popular chains for launchpads including Pump.fun and LetsBONK.fun.
-
Staking: Holders delegate tokens to validators to earn a yield while securing the underlying blockchain infrastructure.
-
Decentralized Finance (DeFi): Users trade, lend, or borrow assets through automated DeFi applications like Jupiter or Raydium.
-
Digital Collectibles: The network hosts a large market for non-fungible tokens (NFTs), which are unique digital assets representing art, media, or identity.
-
DePIN: Solana powers projects in the Decentralized Physical Infrastructure Networks space, such as Helium, which use tokens to incentivize the rollout of real-world hardware.
How Does Solana Work?
Solana operates on a Proof of Stake model combined with a innovation called Proof of History (PoH).
In traditional blockchains, nodes must talk back and forth to agree on what time a transaction occurred, creating bottlenecks.
Solana eliminates this by having a built-in "clock" that creates a digital proof of the passage of time.
Because every node can trust this internal timeline, the network can organize transactions and process them in parallel—running multiple tasks at once across CPU cores—rather than processing them in a single file line.
Team Info and Investors
Solana was founded in 2017 by Anatoly Yakovenko, a former engineer at Qualcomm and Dropbox, who authored the original whitepaper.
He was joined by Greg Fitzgerald, Raj Gokal, and Stephen Akridge to form Solana Labs.
The project is supported by the Solana Foundation, a non-profit based in Switzerland.
Major institutional investors include Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Polychain Capital, Multicoin Capital, and Jump Crypto.
